pr_title: Fix accumulation of tags when testing manifest with wildcard export
pr_body:
# PR Summary

Resets the `Tags`-list in `PSModuleInfo` that survives the shallow clone when getting moduleinfo from scriptanalysiscache.

## PR Context

Currently on repeated calls to `Test-ModuleManifest` for modules with wildcard-export, the module manifest will return duplicate tags which keep accumulating every time.

Fix #17694

comments: Can't reproduce in 7.2.5. Tested on Windows with manifest for both a loaded and unloaded module. Could you provide a minimal sample manifest?

> Can't reproduce in 7.2.5. Tested on Windows with manifest for both a loaded and unloaded module. Could you provide a minimal sample manifest?

Attached temp.zip with minimal sample shown in the screenshot below
[Temp.zip](https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/files/9175151/Temp.zip)
![grafik](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/97656046/180632731-0ff113cc-b2e8-4f8e-be83-d1b0f96b6574.png)

Thanks, can repro now. It occurs only when you:
- Have a `RootModule`
- Use `'*'` in `FunctionsToExport/CmdletsToExport/AliasesToExport`

**Workaround**: Specify `@()` or `@('your values')` in the `...ToExport` entries. It's also better for performance, so win win 🙂

`newModuleInfo` used below is only a [shallow clone of a cached manifest](https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/blob/a468fb1f499f5f6f1468571df76b50e85c9f4b39/src/System.Management.Automation/engine/Modules/ModuleCmdletBase.cs#L6237-L6240) (by filename). So it will keep adding the same tags over and over to an already populated list.

https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/blob/a468fb1f499f5f6f1468571df76b50e85c9f4b39/src/System.Management.Automation/engine/Modules/ModuleCmdletBase.cs#L3233-L3236

Tags is only cleared when `PrivateData` is set, but should always be replaced since tags may have been removed since the last invocation.

Should probably add a internal `ResetTags()` (new list) in `PSModuleInfo` that's called prior to returning the cloned cached manifest to break the reference.
@iSazonov already on it 🙂 Found a similar issue with import while looking into it.

review_comments: Hmm, I wonder why we do this at all if PrivateData is null?

Which one, `$manifestInfo`?

Tbh. I'm confused in general by this massive method as mentioned in https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/issues/17759#issuecomment-1193338559. Hopefully the PowerShell-team can elaborate 🙂
Seems like an alternate fix is for this line to check that `_tags` doesn't already contain the tag to add as duplicates don't make sense anyways.

True. My initial though was `private readonly HashSet<string> _tags = new(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);` but it won't break the reference.

```powershell
New-Item -ItemType File "tagsDemo.psm1"
New-ModuleManifest -Path "tagsDemo.psd1" -RootModule "tagsDemo.psm1" -FunctionsToExport '*' -Tags "hello"

$t = Test-ModuleManifest ./tagsDemo.psd1
New-ModuleManifest -Path "tagsDemo.psd1" -RootModule "tagsDemo.psm1" -FunctionsToExport '*' -Tags "world"

$t2 = Test-ModuleManifest ./tagsDemo.psd1

$t.Tags

# output
hello
world
```
You don't need a HashSet, `List` has a `Contains()` method you can just check against.  You also probably need to clear the `_tags` somewhere so they aren't accumulated across usage.

> You also probably need to clear the `_tags` somewhere so they aren't accumulated across usage.

If I only clear the existing list it would solve the original issue, but not the sample above where the manifest-file has changed and you try to compare two manifest from different points in time.

Breaking the `_tags` reference during shallow clone of the cached entry will fix both the original issue and the scenario above.

> You don't need a HashSet, `List` has a `Contains()` method you can just check against.

`Contains()` wouldn't use case-insensitive comparison. Both alternatives are really solving a different issue though as it changes behavior by deduplicating tags intentionally set in a manifest-file.

I'll happily include it or provide a new PR for that as well if discussion, but imo. that would use case-insensitive comparison. 🙂

> If I only clear the existing list it would solve the original issue, but not the sample above where the manifest-file has changed and you try to compare two manifest from different points in time.
> 
> Breaking the `_tags` reference during shallow clone of the cached entry will fix both the original issue and the scenario above.

Ignore this. Running `Test-ModuleManifest` against different versions of the same manifest-file is broken multiple places due to the cached copy, so fixing tags alone won't achieve much by itself. 🙂 

I can update the PR, but waiting on response on the second part first. Would be easy to dedup intentional duplicates at the same time.
